record.original_question: Give a geometric explanation of the concept of mirror symmetry for Calabi-Yau manifolds that is mathematically complete and conceptually satisfactory.

evidence.quote: Give a geometric full explanation of the concept of mirror symmetry for Calabi-Yau manifolds

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Calabi–Yau n-fold is a compact Kähler manifold X of complex dimension n with vanishing first Chern class (equivalently, admitting a Ricci-flat Kähler metric and a nowhere-vanishing holomorphic n-form). Mirror symmetry is the empirically observed phenomenon that Calabi–Yau n-folds come in pairs (X, X^∨) such that the symplectic geometry (A-model) of X is equivalent to the complex geometry (B-model) of X^∨, and vice versa; concrete shadows of this include the interchange of Hodge numbers h^{p,q}(X) = h^{n-p,q}(X^∨), the enumerative predictions of Candelas–de la Ossa–Green–Parkes relating Gromov–Witten invariants of X to period integrals on X^∨, Kontsevich's homological mirror symmetry equivalence D^b Fuk(X) ≃ D^b Coh(X^∨), and the Strominger–Yau–Zaslow proposal that mirror pairs admit dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations.

Problem: Provide a mathematically complete and conceptually satisfactory geometric explanation of mirror symmetry for Calabi–Yau manifolds. Concretely, give a precise construction that, for an arbitrary compact Calabi–Yau n-fold X, produces a mirror Calabi–Yau n-fold X^∨ together with a geometric correspondence (for instance via dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations, or via a suitable degeneration / non-archimedean / family Floer construction) from which the predicted equivalences — including the Hodge number exchange, the equality of A-model (Gromov–Witten) invariants of X with B-model (variations of Hodge structure / period) invariants of X^∨, and the homological mirror symmetry equivalence between the derived Fukaya category of X and the derived category of coherent sheaves on X^∨ — can be derived as theorems.
artifact.status_search_result: A fully general, mathematically complete geometric explanation of mirror symmetry for Calabi–Yau manifolds remains open. The Strominger–Yau–Zaslow (SYZ) conjecture, which provides the leading geometric framework, has no agreed-upon precise statement and has only been proved in special cases (e.g., toric Calabi–Yau manifolds, del Pezzo and rational elliptic surfaces, log Calabi–Yau surfaces). Related programs (Gross–Siebert, Kontsevich–Soibelman, family Floer theory) have made substantial progress but do not yet yield a complete geometric proof in general.

status_evidence.title: SYZ conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There is no agreed upon precise statement of the conjecture within the mathematical literature, but there is a general statement expected to be close to the correct formulation.
status_evidence.claim: No precise general formulation/proof of the SYZ geometric explanation of mirror symmetry exists; conjecture remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: SYZ mirror symmetry for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: SYZ mirror symmetry has been established for toric Calabi-Yau manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Special cases such as toric Calabi-Yau manifolds are known.

status_evidence.title: The SYZ mirror symmetry conjecture for del Pezzo surfaces and rational elliptic surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Proves SYZ mirror symmetry for non-compact Calabi-Yau surfaces from del Pezzo and rational elliptic surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial results in specific geometric settings.
